title: Startup: supply-ramp transient startup time against the < 1 ms spec line
claim: spec/topology-survey.md Startup row ("self-starting, < 1 ms") -- the startup-TIME half. Measures, in a single transient per PVT point, how long design/bandgap_core.sch + design/startup_injector.sch takes to bring VOUT up after the supply arrives, on a slow ramp, on a fast ramp, and from the worst case of all: placed *in* the degenerate zero-current state at full supply and asked to leave it. The no-other-stable-state half of the same spec line is the sibling experiment sim/startup-stability/; the +/-1% output-accuracy claim is issue #11.
statistical_convention: N/A (corner-matrix claim, not a distribution claim)

analyses: meas tran t_vdd_s when v(vdds)=2.90 rise=1
meas tran t_ref_s when v(vrefs)=1.05 rise=1
meas tran t_vdd_f when v(vddf)=2.90 rise=1
meas tran t_ref_f when v(vreff)=1.05 rise=1
meas tran t_vdd_g when v(vddg)=2.90 rise=1
meas tran t_ref_g when v(vrefg)=1.05 rise=1
meas tran v_s find v(vrefs) at=2.45e-3
meas tran v_f find v(vreff) at=2.45e-3
meas tran v_g find v(vrefg) at=2.45e-3
meas tran v_n find v(vrefn) at=2.45e-3
meas tran g_n find v(gn) at=2.45e-3
meas tran isg find i(vdeg) at=2.45e-3
meas tran v_s1 find v(vrefs) at=1.45e-3
meas tran v_f1 find v(vreff) at=1.45e-3
meas tran v_g1 find v(vrefg) at=1.45e-3

measurements.name: t_start_s
measurements.note: SLOW RAMP (0 -> vsup in t_slow = 1 ms). Startup time measured the way the spec line means it: from the supply arriving (VDD crossing 2.90 V) to VREF crossing 1.05 V. 2.90 V is used rather than the 2.97 V minimum-supply endpoint so the crossing exists even at the 2.97 V corner, where the ramp only *reaches* 2.97 V. Negative means the reference was already up before the supply finished arriving, which is normal on a slow ramp and is a pass -- hence no lower limit.

measurements.name: t_start_f
measurements.note: FAST RAMP (0 -> vsup in t_fast = 1 us). Same definition. The fast ramp is the case where the loop has no time to follow the supply, so the core is closest to being handed a full rail with every internal node still at zero.

measurements.name: t_start_g
measurements.note: DEGENERATE START -- the case this issue is really about. The supply steps to vsup in 1 ns AND the mirror gate GG is initialised to vsup by the testbench's .ic, i.e. the circuit is placed *in* the zero-current state, at full supply, and asked to leave it. The two ramps above start from GDRV = 0, which is the over-driven side of the loop, not the stuck side, so on their own they would not test the startup circuit at all.

measurements.name: t_abs_s
measurements.note: Absolute time of the slow ramp's VREF crossing from t = 0, bounded by (the 1 ms ramp + the 1 ms spec line + margin). Recorded so a negative t_start_s is never the only number on the page.

measurements.name: vref_s
measurements.note: Settled output after the slow ramp. Sanity band only, NOT the +/-1% spec window (issue #11).

measurements.name: vref_f
measurements.note: Settled output after the fast ramp.

measurements.name: vref_g
measurements.note: Settled output after the degenerate start.

measurements.name: vref_spread
measurements.note: Asserts the three copies converge to the *same* operating point. A startup circuit that left the core in a different (e.g. over-driven) stable state, or that stayed partly engaged on one profile and not another, would show up as a ramp-rate-dependent output. This is the transient counterpart of sim/startup-stability/'s single-crossing claim. DIAGNOSIS (issue #284 / DR-010, 2026-09-23 -- SUPERSEDES the 'underdamped settling tail still ringing at the cold/fast corner' wording this note carried since issue #11, which mis-attributed the residual to the SLOW-ramp copy alone). The failing corners are a fixed-sample-time artifact, and the decisive evidence is a cross-bench comparison against a DC operating-point solve rather than another transient: sim/startup-stability/ sweeps GDRV over 0..VDD at the SAME 45 corners and reports the free-running core+injector's DC equilibrium as vref_dut. At all 13 corners where this check fails in record 20260910-010233-e8e2e46, that DC equilibrium lies strictly INSIDE the interval the three transient copies span: the slow-ramp copy v_s is above it at 13 of 13 (+0.13 to +2.88 mV) and the fast-ramp copy v_f is below it at 13 of 13 (-0.38 to -4.62 mV), with the degenerate-start copy v_g likewise below at 12 of 13 (the exception, sf/27 degC/2.97 V, sits +0.20 mV above). Worst corner sf/-40 degC/3.63 V: vref_dut = 1.221454 V against v_s = 1.223660 V (+2.21 mV) and v_f = v_g = 1.216830 V (-4.62 mV) -- i.e. the slow-ramp copy is approaching from above and the fast/degenerate copies from below, and at the worst corner the fast/degenerate pair carries the LARGER residual, not the slow copy. All three are still settling at at=2.45e-3; none of them is the settled value the other two should be graded against. Combined with sim/startup-stability/'s ncross_su=1 at all 45 corners (a single DC equilibrium exists, in the arbitrarily-slow-ramp limit), that makes 'the three copies converge to one operating point' established and the residual a settling-TIME measurement, not a second stable state. The 1 mV bound is still deliberately NOT loosened and the at=2.45e-3 sample point is still NOT moved -- see vref_converge below for the bounded gate that now tests the convergence claim directly, and DR-010 for why a longer window is disproportionate (the recorded contraction rate puts the window needed to clear the worst corner two orders of magnitude past this bench's own < 1 ms scope). The residual stays charged against issue #11's budget.

measurements.name: vref_spread_early
measurements.note: INFORMATIONAL (deliberately unbounded): the same spread expression as vref_spread, sampled 1 ms earlier at at=1.45e-3 instead of at=2.45e-3. It exists so every record carries, at every corner, the raw material for the question the fixed-sample-time bound cannot answer on its own -- is the spread shrinking, and how fast. Paired with vref_spread it gives a two-point contraction per corner at zero incremental simulation cost (same transient, extra 'meas ... find ... at=' taps), which is what DR-010's 'a longer window is disproportionate' conclusion is derived from rather than asserted. 1.45e-3 is chosen as t_slow + 0.45 ms: past the slow ramp's completion and past its output overshoot peak at every corner, so both samples are on the same monotone settling leg.

measurements.name: vref_converge
measurements.expr: (abs(v_s - v_g) + abs(v_s - v_f)) - (abs(v_s1 - v_g1) + abs(v_s1 - v_f1))
measurements.note: BOUNDED GATE, and the measurement that tests what vref_spread's note has always CLAIMED to test: the three copies must be getting closer together over time, i.e. vref_spread must CONTRACT between at=1.45e-3 and at=2.45e-3. A negative value is convergence. If the three startup conditions were settling toward genuinely different operating points -- the failure mode vref_spread exists to catch -- this difference would be zero or positive no matter how long the window, and this gate would fail where a mere fixed-time magnitude check cannot distinguish 'diverged' from 'not yet arrived'. Added by issue #284 / DR-010 because the pre-existing evidence for convergence was a cross-bench inference (sim/startup-stability/'s DC equilibrium bracketing the copies) rather than something this bench measured itself. The bound is 1e-5 V rather than exactly 0 V: at the 125 degC corners the spread is already at this deck's own print resolution at BOTH sample points, so the sign of a sub-10-uV difference there is numerical, not physical; 10 uV is 1% of the vref_spread bound this gate sits alongside and two orders of magnitude below the >= 1 mV contraction measured at every failing corner.

measurements.name: vref_n
measurements.note: CONTROL, and the measurement sim/README.md insists on: the same degenerate initial condition and the same 1 ns supply step on a core with NO injector attached. It has to stay stuck. If it ever came up on its own, the premise of this issue -- and the value of every other number in this record -- would be wrong, so this is a bounded measurement, not a comment.

measurements.name: gn_n
measurements.note: CONTROL, second half: the no-injector core's mirror gate is still parked up near the supply rail at the end of the transient, i.e. it is stuck in the degenerate state specifically, not merely slow.

measurements.name: isup_g
measurements.note: Settled total supply current of the degenerate-start copy (core + injector). Lower bound proves it really did start; upper bound is the < 50 uA Iq budget from design/device-characterization-summary.md, i.e. the injector is not still sinking current after handing over.

spread_checks.note: Untrimmed output over process and temperature must move by more than 10 mV; a frozen value would indicate the .lib corner or .temp injection stopped taking effect.

notes: Four independent copies of the DUT are simulated in one transient so a PVT point costs one ngspice invocation: slow ramp, fast ramp, degenerate start, and the no-injector control. They share only the ground node, and each has its own supply source, so they cannot interact through a rail.

The transient runs with UIC: every node starts at 0 V except the two mirror gates the testbench's .ic places at the supply rail. There is no .nodeset and no preloaded operating point -- contrast sim/bandgap-smoke/, which had to seed the solver onto the intended branch because no startup circuit existed yet. Not needing that seed is itself part of what this experiment demonstrates.
t_slow = 1 ms and t_fast = 1 us are deck params rather than schematic constants so the same testbench can be re-run at other ramp rates (issue #11 reuses these benches) without editing the schematic.

A corner where a 'meas ... when' finds no crossing writes no vector, and the runner records the measurement as missing, i.e. as a failure. That is the intended behaviour: a corner that does not start inside the transient window is a failing corner, not an absent one.

Design vintage split. 20260803-115923-e599e30 and 20260803-124933-e599e30 were minted on feature/issue-10 at e599e30, before the error-amp resize of issue #9 / PR #41: their netlist snapshots carry .param amp_m_in=2, i.e. an amplifier the design no longer ships, so their startup times are not a claim about anything currently in design/. 20260803-204350-f41373d is the re-run against what main actually ships (amp_m_in=16 plus the issue-#52 railed-branch clamp MNC in design/startup_injector.sch) and is the CURRENT record; it supersedes 20260803-124933-e599e30. The < 1 ms line survives the vintage change with room to spare -- worst t_start over all 12 corners and all three ramp profiles is +146 us (ss/125 degC/2.97 V, slow ramp) against the 1 ms bound -- but the sign of t_start_s flips positive at the 125 degC corners where it used to be negative, i.e. on the shipped amp the reference no longer finishes coming up before a 1 ms supply ramp does. That is a change in margin, not in verdict, and it is why t_abs_s exists as a separate bounded measurement: it moved from 0.45 ms to 1.12 ms worst case against its 2.2 ms bound. See sim/startup-ramp/README.md for the record index.

This experiment's overall verdict has been FAIL in every record so far, on vref_spread alone -- at the two ff/-40 degC corners in the early records, at 13 of 45 corners in the post-#193 record 20260910-010233-e8e2e46 -- and never on a startup time. Read the per-measurement verdicts, not the overall line, when asking whether the < 1 ms spec row is substantiated; see the vref_spread note for why the bound is deliberately not being loosened to turn that FAIL into a PASS.

WHAT THIS BENCH DOES AND DOES NOT GRADE AGAINST THE RATIFIED SPEC (issue #284). DR-005's ratified Startup row is 'self-starting, < 1 ms'. Its two halves are the no-other-stable-state claim (sibling bench sim/startup-stability/, PASS 45/45) and the startup-TIME claim (t_start_s / t_start_f / t_start_g here, PASS at every corner of every record this bench has ever produced). vref_spread is NOT one of those halves: it is an additional consistency check this bench invented on top of them, with a bound (1 mV) that no ratified row states. That is not a reason to drop or loosen it -- it catches a real failure mode and it stays graded -- but it IS the reason design/block-characterization-report.md rows 8c/8d must report the two separately rather than rolling a vref_spread FAIL up as a failure of the < 1 ms line. See DR-010.

Issue #284 / DR-010 (2026-09-23) added three 'meas ... find ... at=1.45e-3' taps (v_s1/v_f1/v_g1) and the two measurements they feed, vref_spread_early (informational) and vref_converge (bounded). No existing measurement, bound, deck parameter or sample point changed, and the tran window is unchanged at 2.5 ms: the taps read the trajectory that was already being solved, so a record made with them costs the same per corner as one made without them and stays directly comparable to 20260910-010233-e8e2e46. This is deliberate -- the alternative considered and rejected in DR-010 was extending the window, which a measured 10-corner sensitivity check showed buys only a ~20-25% spread reduction (clearing 1 of 13 failing corners) for ~38% more simulation time per corner.
